blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: For which of these jobs does the page consider plain SHA-256 a suitable tool?

options.text: Storing user passwords so that later logins can be checked against them
options.says: The page says to hash passwords with bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2, since SHA-256 alone is insufficient for them.

options.text: Generating session tokens that an attacker cannot predict or guess
options.says: Tokens come from SecureRandom, the page says, never from a predictable source.

options.text: Checking that a downloaded archive matches the one that was published
options.says: SHA-256 and SHA-512 are suitable for data integrity checks such as checksums and fingerprints.

questions.stem: A service keeps one Cipher in a field and lets all its request threads use it. What does the page say about this?

options.text: Give each thread its own instance, for example through a ThreadLocal
options.says: Cipher, like MessageDigest, Signature and Mac, is not thread-safe: create new instances per thread or use ThreadLocal.

options.text: Share it across threads once init() has run, as its state is then fixed
options.says: The page lists Cipher among the engine classes whose instances are not thread-safe.

options.text: Share it across threads for decryption, as decrypting leaves it unchanged
options.says: The page makes no exception for decryption: Cipher instances are not thread-safe.

concepts: MessageDigest, Cipher, Signature and Mac instances are not thread-safe: one per thread or a ThreadLocal.
SHA-256 suits integrity checks; passwords need bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2, and tokens need SecureRandom.
